column3: NASB supplies “there went up,” which comes from verse 6.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
“The priest the chief” is rendered “the chief priest.”
“According to the hand of” is rendered “because the hand of … was upon him.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
“The beginning of the going up” is rendered “he began to go up.”
“Directed” is rendered “set,” and “to do” as “to practice.” “Decree and judgment” is rendered “His statutes and ordinances.”
“The letter” is rendered “the decree,” and “scribe of the matters of” as “learned in the words of.”
From here to verse 26 the text is Aramaic. “Perfect” is rendered “perfect peace”; the meaning of the Aramaic word is uncertain.
“Who volunteers” is rendered “who are willing.”
“From before the king” is rendered “by the king.”
“His abode” is rendered “whose dwelling.”
Close to the Aramaic.
“This silver” is rendered “this money,” and “drink offerings” as “libations.”
Close to the Aramaic.
“Worship” is rendered “service,” and “make complete” as “deliver in full.”
“The house of the treasures of the king” is rendered “the royal treasury.”
NASB adds “even I”; “diligently let it be done” is rendered “it shall be done diligently.”
“Salt which is not writing” is rendered “salt as needed.”
“Exactly” is rendered “with zeal”; the question “why should there be wrath” is rendered “so that there will not be wrath.”
“The temple servants” is rendered “Nethinim,” and “gatekeepers” as “doorkeepers.” “Not authorized” is rendered “not allowed.”
“Judges and judges” is rendered “magistrates and judges.”
“The decree of the king” is rendered “the law of the king,” and “diligently” as “strictly.”
The text returns to Hebrew. “Beautify” is rendered “adorn.”
“Covenant loyalty” is rendered “lovingkindness.” “I strengthened myself” is rendered “I was strengthened,” and “chiefs” as “leading men.”
